title: Russo-Georgian War
summary: Five days of fighting in August 2008 between Georgia and Russia with the separatist forces of South Ossetia and Abkhazia, opened by a Georgian attempt to retake Tskhinvali and answered by a Russian advance into Georgia proper. It ended with a French-brokered ceasefire, Russian recognition of the two territories as states, and Russian garrisons in both. It is usually called the first European war of the twenty-first century, and its lasting significance is the precedent: force used against a neighbour that had been promised eventual membership of NATO, and no consequence for it that outlasted the season.
